expected_level_description: You can: - show an awareness of Agile methodology and the ways to apply the principles in practice - take an open-minded approach - explain why iteration is important - iterate quickly

You can: - turn complex data into compelling, clear and actionable stories - share data communication skills with the team and across government - present analysis and visualisations in clear ways to communicate complex messages - communicate negative and positive information to stakeholders - give tactical and strategic recommendations

You can: - develop appropriate governance and assurance processes - identify and recommend improvements to governance and assurance processes - support others in following or applying governance and assurance processes

You can: - understand the environment and prioritise the most important or high value tasks - use data to inform planning - manage complex internal and external dependencies - provide delivery confidence - remove blockers or impediments that affect plans and can develop a plan for difficult situations - ensure that teams plan appropriately for their capacity

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders
You can: - work within a strategic context and communicate how activities meet strategic goals - contribute to the development of strategy and policies

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - manage projects from start to close, controlling scope, time, cost, and quality - manage risks, issues, dependencies, and change control - report to project boards and manage suppliers
You can: - run the risk process for a directorate or programme - assess risks against the risk appetite and escalate them - report on risks to committees
You can: - support committee meetings, papers, and minutes - keep governance registers up to date
You can: - supervise day-to-day work and give feedback - take part in recruitment and induction - hold regular one-to-one conversations
